text: Eleven cases of deep puncture wounds of the foot and their complications were reviewed. More than half of the patients had foreign materials introduced at the time of the injury, but these materials were not completely removed initially. The morbidity with these "simple puncture wounds" can indeed be quite prolonged. The authors conclude that meticulous attention to detail during the initial evaluation in the emergency room or physician's office and prompt aggressive treatment of these wounds will prevent serious sequelae in many instances.
